prompts.text: Put the steps of Dijkstra's algorithm in order.
prompts.hint: Before exploring anything, initialize the starting distances.
prompts.explanation: Dijkstra sets initial distances, repeatedly extracts the closest unvisited node, relaxes its outgoing edges, and marks it visited.
items: Set the source distance to 0 and every other distance to infinity
Pick the unvisited node with the smallest known distance
Relax the edges leaving that node
Mark the node visited and repeat until all nodes are done

prompts.text: Put the steps of Kruskal's algorithm in order.
prompts.hint: Begin by arranging all available connections by cost.
prompts.explanation: Kruskal sorts all edges by weight and greedily selects non-cycling edges until V - 1 edges form the spanning tree.
items: Take the cheapest edge that is left
Skip that edge if it would create a cycle
Stop once the tree has V - 1 edges

prompts.text: Which algorithm solves a different problem from the other three?
prompts.hint: Three of these construct a tree connecting all vertices with minimal total cost.
prompts.explanation: Kruskal, Prim, and Borůvka compute minimum spanning trees, whereas Dijkstra computes single-source shortest paths.

prompts.text: Which algorithm has a different worst-case time complexity from the other three?
prompts.hint: Three of these algorithms run in linear time relative to vertices and edges.
prompts.explanation: BFS, DFS, and Kosaraju run in linear O(V + E) time, whereas Floyd-Warshall runs in cubic O(V^3) time.
